newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Mar 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Mar 10.

text.p: The cause of an explosion that killed two Singaporean soldiers near Waiouru on Sunday and wounded 12 others, including a New Zealander, was unclear, a New Zealand Army spokesman said on Sunday. Lieutenant Colonel Colin Richardson said a 50-kilogram, 155-millimetre artillery shell exploded in the breach of a medium-range gun during a live firing exercise just after 10 am, three kilometres south of Waiouru at Robinson's Pond. The New Zealand Army's largest artillery round is 105mm. Page 1.

National MP John Banks, who has complained he was threatened and assaulted by Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters, was responsible for a similar incident five years ago. Banks was the instigator of an incident in November 1992 in which Labour MP Mike Moore complained to the Speaker Sir Robin Gray that Banks -- then police minister -- had abused and threatened his press secretary Paul Jackman. Page 2.

New Zealanders deserved better than macho brawling by politicians in Parliament's corridors, Labour leader Helen Clark said on Sunday. Clark, who returned to New Zealand on Sunday from meetings in Madrid and London, said NZ First's "bully boy" style of politics was unaccaptable. She said New Zealanders deserved better than the incident between NZ First leader Winston Peters and National MP John Banks in which Banks said Peters assaulted him. Page 2.

Managing the relationship between the Coalition partners will take a lot of time, patience and steady hands at the tiller, leader of the House Wyatt Creech says. Creech is chairman of the Coalition Management Committee, which has its first meeting on Thursday. The committee's establishment is timely, considering last Wednesday's fracas between Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters and National MP John Banks -- the worst in a series of embarrassing slip-ups and mismanagement between the Coalition parties. New Zealand's first MMP coalition government could be expected to have teething problems, Creech said. Page 2.

Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters said on Sunday that he had three witnesses who could say Alliance leader Jim Anderton was not present at last Wednesday night's fracas at Parliament. Speaker Doug Kidd is due to rule tomorrow whether there is evidence of a breach of parliamentary rules over the incident, in which MP John Banks said Peters grabbed his collar and pushed and threatened him outside the debating chamber. Page 2.

Government spending "slippage" could collide with declining tax revenues, putting tax cuts after 1998 and government surpluses at risk, analysts of last week's Budget policy statement said. Despite rating Treasurer Winston Peters's first Budget policy statement a mild positive, ANZ said in its weekly commentary that there was a continuing risk of further spending "slippage" and falling income. Page 21.

Politicians, finance and investment houses and corporate bosses will put New Zealand's investment environment under the microscope at a conference in Auckland during the next few days. Representatives from some of the world's leading investment firms will be there to learn the benefits debt and equity can provide for investors. Organisers say the converence will provide visitors with an opportunity to explore the results of the centre-right Coalition. Page 21.
